evidence: Abstract: 'proposing a virtual API server and stable evaluation system. The virtual API server contains a caching system and API simulators which are complementary to alleviate the change in API status.' Authors Guo, Cheng, Wang, ... Liu; arXiv 2403.07714 (v5 Mar 2025).
correction: Venue: arXiv preprint (Findings of ACL 2024 [verify]); full title 'StableToolBench: Towards Stable Large-Scale Benchmarking on Tool Learning of Large Language Models'.

evidence: Abstract: '9 day-to-day apps operable via 457 APIs ... It supports robust programmatic evaluation with state-based unit tests, allowing for different ways of completing a task while also checking for unexpected changes'. Comments: ACL'24 Camera Ready.
correction: Venue: ACL 2024. Note unit tests check final state and collateral damage, 750 tasks.

evidence: Abstract: 'ToolSandbox includes stateful tool execution, implicit state dependencies between tools, a built-in user simulator supporting on-policy conversational evaluation and a dynamic evaluation strategy'. Lu, Holleis, ... Pang (Apple); arXiv 2408.04682.

Page (BFCL V4, updated 2026-04-12): 'evaluates the LLM's ability to call functions (aka tools) accurately'; v1 introduced AST metric; V3 multi-turn blog: state-based evaluation checks 'end state, or end result, should be consistent with ground truth'.
correction: Quote verified, but 'not result correctness' is overstated: BFCL's single-turn categories score call accuracy via AST matching, while V3 multi-turn adds state-based checks of backend end state and V4 adds agentic (web-search/memory) evaluation. Claim instead: BFCL primarily scores whether the model issues correct calls; it assumes tools themselves return correct data and does not test tool-side faults.

evidence: Abstract: 'due to the dynamic nature of external environments, these tools and APIs may become outdated over time, preventing LLMs from correctly invoking tools ... we introduce ToolQA-D, a benchmark specifically designed to evaluate the impact of tool variability.'
correction: Venue: ICLR 2025 (comments: 'Camera ready version for ICLR 2025'); cite year 2025. Authors Guoxin Chen et al.

evidence: Abstract: 'Compared to knowledge editing for facts encoded in text, success here is more challenging: a code LLM must correctly reason about the semantics of the modified function'; synthetic updates to 54 functions, 670 examples.
correction: Authors Zeyu Leo Liu, Shrey Pandit, Xi Ye, Eunsol Choi, Greg Durrett; arXiv preprint (comments: 'Under Review').

evidence: Abstract: '116 Python code completion problems, each conditioned on specific library versions and accompanied by executable unit tests ... GPT-4o achieves a pass@10 of only 39.9% (43.7% when provided with error feedback)'.
correction: Full title 'GitChameleon: Unmasking the Version-Switching Capabilities of Code Generation Models'; Islah et al.; arXiv preprint cs.SE (v1 numbers).

evidence: Abstract: 'reveals that version-controllable code generation is indeed a significant challenge, even for GPT-4o and other strong frontier models.' Tasks: version-specific code completion and version-aware code migration; metric CDC@1.
correction: Claim should cover both tasks (completion and migration), not migration alone. Venue: arXiv preprint.
